title: Domain IV: Procurement Business Principles - Procurement Business Principles - External Resources
subject: Procurement Business Principles

questions.q: In public procurement, 'benchmarking' is best defined as:
options: Requiring all vendors to provide free samples before awarding a contract.
Comparing an agency's processes, performance metrics, and practices against those of recognized industry leaders or similar organizations.
Setting a fixed, non-negotiable price for all goods.
Using the lowest price received as the standard for all future purchases.
questions.explain: Benchmarking involves measuring an organization's key performance indicators (cycle time, cost per PO, etc.) against best-in-class peers to identify areas for improvement.
questions.subject: Procurement Business Principles

questions.q: A buyer is drafting a complex RFP for an unfamiliar software system. What is an appropriate and effective use of external professional resources?
options: Paying a single software vendor to write the RFP in exchange for a guaranteed award.
Reaching out to peer agencies or via a professional network (like NIGP) to request sample RFPs and lessons learned.
Copying a peer agency's RFP word-for-word, including their specific state laws, without review.
Skipping the RFP process and using an external auditor to choose the system.
questions.explain: Networking with peer agencies and using professional association resources provides valuable templates, specifications, and lessons learned without compromising competition or legality.
questions.subject: Procurement Business Principles

questions.q: What is the fundamental difference between 'piggybacking' and a 'joint solicitation' cooperative contract?
options: Piggybacking is illegal, while joint solicitations are legal.
In a joint solicitation, multiple agencies combine their requirements into one bid upfront; piggybacking involves adopting a contract already competitively bid and awarded by another agency.
Joint solicitations can only be done at the federal level.
Piggybacking requires the requesting agency to sign a completely new contract with different terms.
questions.explain: Joint solicitations combine volume prior to bidding. Piggybacking utilizes an existing contract post-award, provided the original contract included cooperative language.
questions.subject: Procurement Business Principles

questions.q: Before utilizing a cooperative purchasing agreement (piggybacking) from another state, the procurement officer's most critical legal responsibility is to ensure that:
options: The vendor is physically headquartered in the officer's state.
The originating agency's solicitation process complied with the procurement statutes and competitive requirements of the officer's own jurisdiction.
The prices are at least 50% lower than current retail prices.
The contract is completely exempt from public records laws.
questions.explain: An agency can only utilize a cooperative contract if the original lead agency's competitive process met or exceeded the statutory requirements of the piggybacking agency's jurisdiction.
questions.subject: Procurement Business Principles

questions.q: Which entity is defined as the 'Lead Agency' in a national cooperative purchasing program?
options: The agency that pays the membership fee.
The public entity that conducts the competitive solicitation, evaluates responses, and awards the master contract.
The vendor who receives the award.
The federal government oversight committee.
questions.explain: The Lead Agency is the governmental body that actually issues the solicitation, conducts the evaluation, and establishes the resulting master agreement that other agencies can use.
questions.subject: Procurement Business Principles

questions.q: An agency issues a Request for Information (RFI) regarding electric sanitation trucks. The primary objective of using this external market resource is to:
options: Award a contract to the best respondent.
Gather information about the availability, specifications, and industry standards for a commodity before drafting a formal solicitation.
Determine the lowest price in the market to skip bidding.
Penalize vendors who do not respond.
questions.explain: An RFI is a non-binding market research tool used to gather knowledge about industry trends, technical capabilities, and potential suppliers before finalizing a solicitation strategy.
questions.subject: Procurement Business Principles

questions.q: What is a major organizational benefit of procurement professionals participating in external associations like NIGP or NASPO?
options: Guaranteeing annual budget increases.
Accessing standardized best practices, model legislation, and continuous professional development.
Allowing associations to legally sign contracts on behalf of the agency.
Bypassing state ethical standards.
questions.explain: Professional associations establish industry standards, offer certification, provide networking, and disseminate model best practices to elevate the profession.
questions.subject: Procurement Business Principles

questions.q: A procurement office creates an 'Interlocal Agreement.' What is the typical purpose of this document?
options: To finalize a contract between the city and a private corporation.
To establish a legal framework allowing two or more government entities to share resources or purchase cooperatively.
To outline the grievance process for agency employees.
To waive the requirement for public bidding.
questions.explain: An Interlocal Agreement (or intergovernmental agreement) is a contract between two or more public agencies to cooperate on mutual issues, often including cooperative purchasing.
questions.subject: Procurement Business Principles

questions.q: When comparing cooperative contracts to conduct 'due diligence,' a buyer should carefully review the master contract for 'administrative fees.' Why is this important?
options: To ensure the fee is paid directly to the buyer as a commission.
Because the fee is typically built into the vendor's pricing, and the buyer needs to determine if the contract truly offers the best value.
Because administrative fees make the contract illegal.
To force the vendor to remove the fee before order placement.
questions.explain: Cooperative programs often charge a fee to the vendor (e.g., 1-2% of sales) which is passed onto the purchasing agency in the item cost. Due diligence determines if the combined price remains the best value compared to an independent bid.
questions.subject: Procurement Business Principles

questions.q: To effectively use external benchmarking metrics like 'Cost to Produce a PO,' the agency must ensure:
options: The comparing organizations are within the exact same zip code.
They define the variables identically to the benchmarked organizations (comparing apples to apples).
The agency has a bigger budget than the benchmarked organization.
They only benchmark against private sector companies.
questions.explain: For benchmarking to be valid and actionable, organizations must use consistent definitions and methodologies to measure their processes (e.g., what specific costs are included in a PO).
